entry.title: Network Menu Speed Test 1.0
entry.content:
Network Menu Speed Test

Windows 11's network menu ("Run internet speed test") opens

https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2324916

in the default browser, which redirects to a Bing search page.

This mod intercepts that URL in the shell processes and replaces it with a native flyout. The window, the gauge, the result cards and the speed measurement all live inside the mod: no external application or protocol handler is involved. The test talks to the public Cloudflare speed test endpoints (speed.cloudflare.com), the same stateless endpoints used by the website.

Screenshots

Light theme Dark theme
Desktop Acrylic Results card

Data usage

The test transfers real data with a per-direction budget of 512 MB. Lines at or below ~340 Mbps complete the full 12 s window per direction without reaching the budget; faster lines end the phase once the budget is spent (minimum 4 s window, and the result divides bytes by the time the transfer was actually moving data). Total usage stays under ~1 GB regardless of line speed, and the results card shows the bytes used ("Data used: 762 MB", also included in the clipboard text).

The Start the test automatically setting defaults to auto: the test starts when the flyout opens, except when Windows reports the connection as metered - then the flyout opens idle and waits for a click on Start.

Coexistence: the mod perform-speedtest-redirect intercepts the same URL launches. If both are enabled, whichever mod hooks the launch first wins - disable the other one to keep this mod's flyout.

The flyout opens above the taskbar, on the monitor under the mouse. It closes when you click outside, but never while a measurement is running.

It is keyboard accessible (Tab / Enter / Esc with a WinUI-style focus ring), exposed to screen readers through MSAA (WM_GETOBJECT), and honours the "Animation effects" system setting: with animations off every transition is instant. The error view shrinks the window to fit its content.

Settings

  • Extra URL patterns: additional substrings separated by |.
  • Fall back to the web page: if the flyout cannot start, run the original URL instead of doing nothing.
  • Also intercept browser process launches: catch the network menu launching the browser directly through CreateProcessW. The launch returns ERROR_CANCELLED because no browser process is created; turning it off makes the menu open the browser normally when the shell skips the shell-execute path.
  • Start the test automatically: auto starts the test when the flyout opens, but waits for a click when Windows reports the connection as metered; always starts unconditionally; never always waits for a click.
  • Language: auto (follows the Windows display language), it or en.

Diagnostics go to the Windhawk mod log: enable logging for this mod from its Details page in Windhawk when you need them.

Note: when the network menu launches the browser directly through CreateProcessW, the flyout is shown but process creation returns ERROR_CANCELLED: the hook never reports success without creating the requested browser process.

entry.title: Bluetooth No Sleep 1.0.0
entry.content:
Bluetooth No Sleep (Bluetooth Audio Keep-Alive)

A lightweight Windows background utility and Windhawk tool mod that prevents Bluetooth audio devices (headphones, wireless earbuds, soundbars, DACs, and speakers) from falling asleep, dropping initial playback, or disconnecting during silence.

Why this mod?

Modern Bluetooth audio peripherals employ aggressive power-saving timers:

  1. Initial Audio Truncation: When no audio plays for a few seconds, the device enters a low-power state and shuts off its internal DAC/amplifier. When audio resumes, waking up takes 1-2 seconds, dropping the beginning of system notifications, speech, or media playback.
  2. Pops and Static Bursts: Rapid DAC wakeups often create audible transients, clicks, or static bursts ("pink noise").
  3. Unsolicited Idle Disconnections: Many wireless devices shut down completely after 5 to 10 minutes of silence, forcing manual power cycling.

How it works

This mod uses Windows Audio Session API (WASAPI) Shared Mode to continuously stream an inaudible digital silence buffer (0x00 PCM or sub-audible dither) to the active audio endpoint:

  • Non-Intrusive Shared Mode: Runs alongside your normal applications without monopolizing or locking audio devices.
  • Event-Driven Endpoint Tracking: Uses IMMNotificationClient to monitor device transitions. When your default audio device switches or a Bluetooth headset reconnects, it rebinds automatically without crashes.
  • Near-Zero CPU Overhead: Uses buffer-synchronized wait events and sleep cycles to keep CPU usage below 0.1%.
  • Optional Inactivity Gate: Can automatically pause the keep-alive stream after prolonged user inactivity to allow intentional battery conservation and permit normal Windows system sleep (powercfg /requests).
  • Dedicated Tool Mod: Runs inside windhawk.exe as a dedicated background tool without injecting into or hooking any system processes.

entry.title: Explorer Core Context Menu Customizer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Core Context Menu Customizer

Windows does not provide any registry entries or built-in options to customize the icons or labels of core File Explorer context menu commands. This mod was created to fill that gap cleanly and safely.

Windows 11 Note: This mod customizes the classic File Explorer context menu (accessible via Show more options or Shift+F10, or when the classic context menu is enabled).

Screenshots:

Disabled (Default) Enabled (Customized)

Highlights:

  • Canonical Verb Matching: Identifies core shell commands via IContextMenu::GetCommandString (GCS_VERBW), working across every Windows display language without touching third-party shell extension items.
  • Zero Layout Distortion: Attaches icons cleanly during IContextMenu::QueryContextMenu so native row height, padding, and bold text remain completely untouched.
  • Clear-to-Reset Behavior: Clearing an icon path removes the icon for Open, Delete, Rename, or Properties, while Run as administrator reverts to the native Windows UAC shield.
  • Custom Icon Support: Easily add your own .ico files or use any built-in Windows icon with dll,index syntax.
  • Per-Monitor DPI & Leak-Free Caching: Caches 32-bpp ARGB bitmaps per monitor DPI in memory with zero GDI handle leaks.

Dynamic %file% Placeholder:

Include %file% (or %name%) in any custom label field to dynamically display the right-clicked file, folder, or shortcut target name. Names longer than 30 characters are automatically shortened to the first 30 characters followed by ...:

  • Rename: '%file%' -> Rename: 'Spotify.exe'
  • Open: %file% -> Open: New folder (2)
  • Delete %file% -> Delete Very_Long_File_Name_Over_Thirt...
  • %file% Properties -> report.pdf Properties

Supported Context Menu Items:

  1. Open (open) - Top bold default action (default icon: imageres.dll,-185)
  2. Run as administrator (runas) - UAC elevation action (keeps native UAC shield and default label unless customized)
  3. Delete (delete) - File and folder deletion action (default icon: Full Recycle Bin imageres.dll,-54)
  4. Rename (rename) - Inline rename action (default icon: Clipboard shell32.dll,-16763, default label: Rename: '%file%')
  5. Properties (properties) - Bottom item details action (default icon: imageres.dll,-114)

entry.title: Flip3DComp 2.0
entry.content:
Flip3DComp

Original version by: ALTaleX531

A DirectComposition reimplementation of the Flip3D Window switcher introduced on Windows Vista, for newer versions of Windows. Ported from my repository Flip3DComp

Demo

Live window previews follow the original Flip3D carousel layout and timing.

Requirements

  • Windows 10 versions 1703 and higher
  • Windhawk 1.7.3 or higher

⚠️ Notes

  • The optional Task View override currently uses the Windows 11 Task View activation path on AMD64. It is unavailable on x86, ARM64 & Windows 10.
  • Do not enable more than one Win+Tab replacement. Disable Any mods that override Win+Tab, or leave Win+Tab disabled in Alt+Tab Flip 3D, while using Flip3DComp.

Controls

  • Win+Tab: Open Flip3D
  • Ctrl + Win + Tab: Open Flip3D in Sticky Mode
  • Tab / Shift + Tab, arrow keys, mouse wheel: scroll the carousel
  • Enter or left click a card: activate the selected window
  • Home: return to the original front window
  • Esc: exit
  • F5: replay the enter animation

Mod disclosure

  • Unlike the existing Flip 3D mods in the Windhawk catalog, this mod is a reimplementation of the original Windows Vista Flip 3D, built on DirectComposition.

entry.title: Glass Widget Bar 0.3.0
entry.content:
Glass Widget Bar

A desktop widget bar that sits in a frosted-glass frame: the blurred wallpaper shows through a soft, dark-tinted rounded panel with thin light edges. The widgets have no glass of their own; they are drawn straight onto the frame and separated by thin dividers.

Widget What it does
Clock Analog clock with an orange second hand
Calendar Weekday, large day number, month grid; today is highlighted in red
Music The track that is playing right now (Spotify, browser, Media Player...), cover art, progress and ⏮ ⏯ ⏭ buttons

Languages

Labels, day names and month names follow your Windows display language automatically. You can also pick a language in the settings.

English, Türkçe, Deutsch, Français, Español, Italiano, Português (Brasil), Nederlands, Polski, Русский, Українська, Čeština, Svenska, Dansk, Norsk bokmål, Suomi, Ελληνικά, Magyar, Română, Български, Bahasa Indonesia, Tiếng Việt, ไทย, हिन्दी, 日本語, 한국어, 简体中文, 繁體中文.

Other display languages fall back to English. The first day of the week in the calendar follows your Windows regional format (or the chosen language). Right-to-left languages are not supported yet. The translations are machine-assisted, corrections are welcome.

Notes

  • The default layer is the desktop: windows cover the bar. Press the hotkey (default Ctrl+Alt+W) to bring it to the front (press again to send it back), or set "Always on top" in the settings.
  • The hotkey, its modifier keys and its key can be changed or turned off in the settings. Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so if your keyboard layout types characters with AltGr, pick a combination without Alt. If another app already owns the combination it cannot be registered; the Windhawk log then says so.
  • Works on the primary monitor only. A picture wallpaper is expected.
  • The defaults of the frame (opacity 15, blur 10) match the dock mod this frame comes from. If your wallpaper is very bright, raise the opacity.
  • The music widget reads the Windows media session, so every app that publishes one is shown.
  • Developed on Windows 11 (64-bit).

Credits and license

The frame (rounded "squircle" corners, edge glow and edge lines) is ported from MacOS Style Dock by Zach Vaughn (GPL-3.0). This mod is therefore released under GPL-3.0 as well.

entry.title: Color Picker / Eyedropper Tool 1.0.2
entry.content:
Color Picker / Eyedropper Tool for Windows 11

A lightweight, system-wide color picker overlay mod for Windhawk, inspired by Microsoft PowerToys Color Picker. Activated by the default keyboard shortcut Win + Alt + C, it allows you to select any pixel on your screen via a customizable global hotkey, view a magnified pixel grid loupe, and automatically obtain the color value in HEX, RGB, HSL, and CMYK formats with one-click clipboard copying.

Features

  • System-Wide Screen Freeze & Overlay: Freezes the screen upon activation to prevent accidental click-throughs onto underlying windows.
  • Magnified Loupe Cursor: Displays a magnified preview grid with a centered crosshair and a live color preview badge that follows your cursor.
  • Multi-Format Support: Automatically converts and displays captured colors in:
    • HEX (e.g., #FF5733 or ff5733)
    • RGB (e.g., rgb(255, 87, 51))
    • HSL (e.g., hsl(11, 100%, 60%))
    • CMYK (e.g., cmyk(0%, 66%, 80%, 0%))
  • Native Windows 11 Dark Mode Support: The result pop-up window automatically adapts to your system theme (Light or Dark mode).
  • Modern UI Styling: Clean, dialog-style UI using Segoe UI font, smooth rounded corners, drop-shadow effects, and single-click copy buttons.
  • Customizable Mod Settings: Directly configure hotkeys and color formatting preferences within the Windhawk UI.

Hotkey & Controls

  • Activate Eyedropper: Default hotkey is Win + Alt + C (customizable in Windhawk settings).
  • Pick Color: Left-Click anywhere on the screen to capture the pixel color and open the copy window.
  • Cancel Eyedropper: Press Escape or Right-Click to exit picking mode without selecting a color.

Configuration Settings

You can customize the mod settings directly from the Windhawk Mod Manager UI:

Setting Type Default Description
Hotkey Key String C Single alphabet character used with Win + Alt (selectable via a dropdown menu).
Include '#' Prefix in HEX Boolean true Choose whether HEX values include the # symbol (#CDCDCD vs CDCDCD).
Uppercase HEX Characters Boolean true Toggle uppercase vs. lowercase HEX characters (#ABCDEF vs #abcdef).

Dependencies & Technical Details

  • Target Process: windhawk.exe (runs as a Windhawk tool mod)
  • Libraries Linked: -lgdi32, -lmsimg32, -ldwmapi, -luxtheme, -lshcore
  • Architecture: Pure Win32 GDI & User32 APIs (no heavy external GUI dependencies).

entry.title: Confetti Spawner 1.4.0
entry.content:
Confetti Spawner

Press a hotkey and a burst of confetti (or color emoji) flies across the monitor under your mouse pointer. Hold the hotkey to keep it going. The effect is drawn on a click-through overlay that never takes focus, so you can keep typing and clicking while it plays.

The overlay only exists while particles are on screen. When the last particle is gone the window is destroyed and the frame timer stops, so the mod uses no CPU while idle.

The mod runs in its own small Windhawk process and does not inject into any other program.

Hotkeys

Default Action
Ctrl+Alt+F10 Fire a burst. Hold the keys to keep firing
none Cycle the origin (sides, top, bottom, cursor, random) and fire
none Cycle the mode (confetti, emoji, mixed) and fire

The cycle hotkeys are off by default. Set them in the settings to use them.

While the mod is enabled, its hotkey combinations are reserved system-wide, so other apps stop receiving them. Pick combinations you don't use elsewhere (for example Ctrl+Shift+C is copy in Windows Terminal). On keyboard layouts with AltGr, AltGr is sent as Ctrl+Alt, so a Ctrl+Alt+<letter> hotkey can block a character you type with AltGr. Function keys are a safe choice.

Hotkeys are written as modifiers plus a key, for example Ctrl+Alt+F10, Alt+F9, Ctrl+Shift+F9 or Ctrl+Alt+Space. Modifiers are Ctrl, Shift, Alt and Win. Keys can be a letter, a digit, F1 to F24, Space, Enter, Tab, Esc, Insert, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, the arrow keys (Up, Down, Left, Right), Num0 to Num9, Pause or PrintScreen. Type none (or leave the field empty) to turn a hotkey off. If another program already owns a combination, it can't be registered; the mod log says so.

Hold to fire: while the fire hotkey (its main key and modifiers) stays held, the mod keeps emitting at the normal rate (particle count per emission time) and stops when you let go. A quick tap still plays one full burst.

Cycling the origin or the mode only lasts until the settings are saved again or the mod restarts. The saved settings are not changed.

Modes

  • Confetti: paper pieces in the shapes and colors you pick. With Flip enabled they tumble in 3D as they fall.
  • Emoji: the emoji from the Emoji list, drawn in full color.
  • Mixed: both at once. Emoji share sets how many of the particles are emoji.

Origins

  • Sides: two cannons in the bottom corners shooting up and inward (the classic look). Side cannon angle sets how steeply they fire: 70 is classic, 90 shoots straight up, lower values shoot flatter toward the middle.
  • Top: confetti rain from the top edge.
  • Bottom: a fountain from the bottom center.
  • Cursor: an explosion from the mouse pointer. Every particle spawns at the pointer position at the moment it is emitted, so moving the mouse while holding the hotkey drags the stream along, even onto another monitor.
  • Random: one of the above, picked per burst.

Settings

The defaults reproduce the original classic confetti: sides origin, 600 rectangular pieces in six colors, no 3D flip, long lifetime.

Windhawk number settings are whole numbers, so decimal values are stored scaled. Each setting's description says how: for example Gravity is in hundredths, so 50 means 0.50, and Drag is in thousandths, so 990 means 0.990.

  • Particle count, Emission time, Speed, Gravity, Spread, Source width: shape of the burst. Emission time is how long a burst keeps spawning particles.
  • Wobble, Size, Spin, Drag: how particles move and look while falling. Drag is the share of velocity kept per 60 Hz tick.
  • Lifetime, Fade, Opacity: how long particles live, whether they fade out over the last quarter of their life, and the overall overlay opacity.
  • Frame rate: animation frame rate. Physics is time based, so the motion looks the same at any frame rate; higher is only smoother.
  • Emoji, Emoji size, Emoji spin: the emoji list is separated by spaces. Joined emoji sequences (such as family or flag emoji) are kept intact.
  • Shapes, Colors: confetti shapes (rect, square, circle, triangle, star, heart) and colors (#RRGGBB). Each list item can also hold several values separated by commas.
  • Preview on save: fire one burst whenever you save the settings, handy while tuning.

Tips

  • Bursts land on the monitor under the pointer and on the virtual desktop you are on.
  • Firing again while a burst is still playing on the same monitor adds to it.
  • Old overlays keep animating until empty after the pointer moves to another monitor.
  • For a snow look, use origin Top, shape circle, color #FFFFFF, gravity 5 and wobble 20.
  • Very high particle counts on 4K monitors cost more GPU and CPU time per frame. A single overlay is capped at 8000 live particles.

entry.title: macOS Gestures - Mission Control 1.3.1
entry.content:
macOS Gestures - Mission Control

Mission Control for Windows. A three-finger swipe up on a precision touchpad opens a live, animated overview of all your windows; the overview follows your fingers the whole way, and springs into place when you let go. Swipe back down, press Esc, or pick a window to leave.

What you get

  • Live window previews (the same technology the taskbar and Alt+Tab use, so videos keep playing) laid out in a clean grid, with the app icon and title under each window.
  • Minimized windows are shown too, and dialogs are drawn on top of the window they belong to.
  • The taskbar slides out of the screen with your fingers and comes back when you pick a window.
  • A virtual desktops bar flush with the bottom edge: see your desktops, switch to one or create a new one. It fades in with the swipe.
  • A close button on the window under the mouse (also the middle mouse button and the Delete key), with the remaining windows gliding to their new places.
  • Keyboard: Esc closes, arrow keys / Tab move the selection, Enter or Space picks it.
  • Spring physics with the finger speed carried over; pushing further up when everything is already open stretches the grid with rubber-band resistance.
  • Respects the Windows "Animation effects" setting, and is switched off over fullscreen apps and games.

Three-finger left / right

Windows only lets a program take over all three-finger swipes at once, so the mod performs the Alt+Tab itself: swipe right for Alt+Tab, left for Alt+Shift+Tab, and keep swiping to keep cycling. It can also be set to do nothing.

Requirements

  • Windows 11 with the touchpad gestures API (TouchpadGesturesController) and a precision touchpad. On builds without that API the mod stays idle and the log says "TouchpadGesturesController not supported".
  • The mod runs only in the shell's explorer.exe (not in folder windows opened in a separate process, nor in Explorer's COM helper processes).

What changes in Windows

  • While the mod runs it takes over all three-finger swipes, so Windows' own three-finger actions are off: swipe up (Task View) and swipe down (show desktop) have no Windows replacement while Mission Control is closed. Turning the mod off gives them back.
  • The left/right swipe sends Alt+Tab as keystrokes. When an app running as administrator has the focus, Windows blocks those keystrokes, so that swipe does nothing there. The desktops bar uses Windows' Win+Ctrl shortcuts the same way and has the same limit.

Conflicts

  • CoverTabby with its touchpad option turned on also takes over three-finger swipes. Use only one of the two for touchpad gestures.

Settings

Everything above can be changed from the Settings tab: background material (Mica, Mica Alt, Acrylic, live blur, blurred wallpaper), swipe distance, which parts to show, and the animation tuning (speed, bounce, stretch, background fade).

Notes

  • The live previews use private DWM functions, which Windows updates can change. If they stop working the mod falls back to the classic thumbnails on its own.
  • Other mods that animate windows closing (like Windows Animations) are kept from playing their animation in front of Mission Control: a window is hidden just before it is closed. Keep that mod's option to animate hidden windows turned off. If the window is still there a moment later (it asked "Save changes?", or it closes to the tray), it is shown again.
  • Mission Control shows up to 24 windows.
  • If the mod does not start at logon, turn on logging in the mod's Advanced tab in Windhawk and check the log output: the start-up steps are logged there.

entry.title: Mac OS 27 Finder Bar 1.1.0
entry.content:
• New Custom liquid glass theme (from Siri Plus Launchpad): your color at the top, fading into clear glass, with a fine line of light along the bottom edge. It works for the panels, the bar's background or both. The color (presets or any color), the strength and how far down the color goes are set in Menu Bar Settings.
  • New Light, Dark and OLED solid themes.
  • Themes everywhere: the bar's theme also styles the menus, the Control Center, the panels and the pills. New Panel theme option gives the menus a theme of their own (with the Clear bar, this choice is also in Customize theme).
  • New Customize theme section (replaces "Glass"): it adjusts the bar's theme, and each glass theme keeps its own settings (transparent ↔ frosted, edge refraction, background blur, live), with a button to restore that theme's defaults. Without "live", Glass and "Window color" use a still, blurred picture of the background.
  • Bar background per display: Customize per display gives each connected display its own background and text color.
  • Notice pills: style follows the bar, or glass, liquid glass, custom liquid glass, light, dark or OLED; text color (theme, white or black); "Live background" for the glass styles.
  • Control Center: the cascade opening now slides each row out from under the row above.
  • Control Center: new "When the Control Center closes" option: cascade, shrink, fade, slide up or none.
  • Notifications: new Notifications choice: Floating (default: the top and each notification in its own glass card, in the Control Center's style, following the theme) or Inside the box. Text color: theme, white or black. The bell is now one of the bar items.
  • Notifications: a round picture on each card. It's the sender's photo when the app saves it on the PC (with the app's icon in the corner), otherwise the app's icon. Icon shape: circle or the macOS icon shape.
  • Notifications: a Reply button on the card for apps that support replies. Clicking a card opens it in the app.
  • Notifications: your replies stay in the card until you clear it, and new messages from the same conversation go into the same card, in order.
  • The volume and brightness pill shows the percentage.
  • Bluetooth: the Bluetooth pill can search for new devices and pair them, without opening Settings. The pairing code shows in the pill (confirm it, or type it on the device), and a failed pairing shows the reason code. Devices that ask you to type a PIN on the PC still need Settings.
  • Now Playing: it stays in the bar and the Control Center while the music is paused, with the cover, and Play resumes it.
  • While the bar's volume indicator is on, Windows' own volume pill is hidden, including the newer pill that the keyboard volume keys show on recent Windows 11 versions. It comes back when the indicator or the mod is turned off.
  • New Disks item (optional): its menu lists the local and removable disks with a usage bar each, and opens them in Explorer.
  • Bar text and icons: automatic (Windows theme, or the solid background), white or black, in Menu Bar Settings.
  • "Show the bar on": all displays, the main one, or a chosen display (listed by name). If that display is disconnected, the bar moves to the main one.
  • Now Playing: clicking the album cover (Control Center or Now Playing) brings the playing app's window to the front.
  • Now Playing: new "Full cover" layout. The cover fills the panel, the text and progress bar sit on a dark gradient at the bottom, and the controls are round glass buttons like the Control Center's, with the cover magnified under each one.
  • Bar icons now share one size: each one is scaled to the same height, and icons and text grow together with one size setting. The bar height is set on its own, with a button to restore the default size.
  • One selection color for the bar, the menus and their switches.
  • The font is picked in Menu Bar Settings (it left Windhawk's settings page).
  • Menu Bar Settings reorganized (bar language, font, themes, size and behavior); its drop-down lists use the window's own glass, and a row reacts only to clicks on its control.
  • Now Playing: the bar icon is a thin round play or pause sign. In the "Full cover" layout, the buttons are white in light glass themes.
  • Menu Bar Settings: the window can be moved from any empty spot and opens where it was left.
  • Notifications: with no notifications, a small "No notifications" pill, like "Edit Controls".
  • Status pills (Caps Lock, Focus, audio output...) show the latest state: a new one of the same kind replaces the text of the one on screen instead of queuing behind it.
  • New option: hide the bar while a window is maximized on its display. The window gets the whole height, and the bar comes back by itself when the window is restored or minimized, or on the desktop.
  • New "Hide with the handle" option: a thin pill at the top center; a click shows the bar and windows move down for it (with the "Window color" background, the bar also takes the color of the active window's title bar); another click hides it. It's invisible while the bar is shown, until you point at it, and grows with a spring animation. While it's on, the other ways of hiding are off; "Hide while maximized" turns it off, since the bar comes back on its own. Hiding when the pointer touches the top was removed.
  • New Window color bar background: transparent over the desktop, and the color of the title bar of the maximized window on that display; the color stays while a menu, Start, search or another window is in front. It replaces "Solid background with a maximized window".
  • Weather: a plain glass look for the widget, and a switch to turn off its animations.
  • Fix: with "Follow the background live", Now Playing and the Notifications panel follow the background too.
  • Fix: after an update or recompile, the bar comes back on its own (before, the mod had to be turned off and on).
  • Fix: with liquid glass, a panel that had just closed (Control Center, calendar, weather, tray) no longer shows up inside the next panel's background.
  • Fix: opening Notifications no longer highlights the camera icon; the bar's highlight stays on the right item.
  • Fix: with liquid glass, panels at the edge of the screen no longer show a clear strip along that edge.
  • Fix: with the liquid bar, the bar no longer reflects the title bar of a maximized window below it.
  • Fix: floating notifications with Glass or "Window color" and live on no longer show glass slivers at the ends of the top pill.
  • Cleanup: removed unused code and translations.
  • README: new demo with zoom on each feature (animated WebP, plus the full-quality MP4).

entry.title: Touchpad Relaxed Hand Tracking 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Improved movement precision: slow movements no longer lose distance, resting fingers drop out of the movement, and a single finger moving on its own leads, for precise positioning.
  • Speed reset: the multipliers are back to 1.5 for 5-3 fingers and 1.0 for 2-1. If you changed them, check your values.
  • Fewer accidental clicks: touches at the pad's edge, a finger flickering back where it just left, and the thumb no longer click.
  • Steadier near the pad's edge: a finger at the edge, which the touchpad reads poorly, rests while fingers further in steer.
  • Thumb recognition: with the new Hand setting (right or left), the thumb is the touch farthest inside the hand on the lower part of the pad, or, with the whole hand down, anywhere. The pinky is never taken for it, and recognition holds when the index crosses over the thumb, a finger slips off the pad and comes back, or the pad reports a flat thumb as two touches.
  • The thumb is left out of the more-fingers glide for better movement precision: it only rests, helps start the glide and counts as a finger for the speed multiplier. It never moves the pointer or clicks while other fingers touch the pad, even when the pad reports it as two touches.
  • Diagnostics overlay: a configurable hotkey shows how the mod reads each finger: which ones steer, rest, may tap, scroll or hold, and which one is the thumb. It can be dragged and closed, and records nothing while hidden.
  • Mouse wheel is now the default scroll output. More precise vertical and horizontal scrolling. Touch scrolling is still available in the settings.
  • Tap and hold feedback (optional): a small dot shows beside the pointer on each tap, and stays while a hold drags or a scroll runs, Windows' own taps and scroll included. The pointer itself doesn't change.

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 3.2.0
entry.content:
New

  • Your commands can run by themselves: give a command a time and days in its editor ("Run by itself, at a time") and it runs while the island is on, as a click would. A notice says if it ran or couldn't, with Try again and, for a command line, Open in terminal. The schedules are looked at once a minute on the island's thread (CheckScheduledCommands): CommandMinutesDue runs the minute it is in (the first one too, and after a sleep) and, at a summer-time change, the minutes the clock skipped (UTC one minute on, the zone in daylight time, the jump its bias), never one twice, also across a restart in the same minute; nothing missed is made up. A failed command line's output is kept for its notice's Open in terminal, which shows it (type) instead of running the line again.
  • The graphics card's use and temperature can go on the pill, next to CPU, RAM and VRAM; a click opens the GPU tab of the usage panel (Apps and tools tab).
  • The charging battery's color can be green as before, like the other icons, Windows' accent or one you pick (System tab, #6816).
  • A Mobile data tile in the control center, only on a PC with a mobile broadband modem; add it with Edit (#6888).
  • A short notice with the cover, title and artist when the song changes; a click opens What's playing (What's playing tab, off by default, #6822).
  • The wheel on what's playing can go the other way round: up is the next song (What's playing tab, off by default, #6822).
  • A banner can close when you click anywhere outside it and the island; calls, alarms and reminders stay until you answer them (Banners tab, off by default, #6822).
  • The Bar can hide to its line too (#7131): with "Hide as its line" and the new "Bar: hide as its line too" on, the Bar shrinks to a thin line on the screen's edge when the mouse is away, and comes back as the mouse reaches the line. Windows then use the strip it kept, and the Bar shows over them.
  • In the Bar, the items can go to the screen's corners without the clock in the middle, like the macOS menu bar: put a separator line in the order (+ Line) and, with "Bar: items at the screen's corners" on and the clock not in the middle, the items before the first line stay at the left corner and the rest, the clock too, at the right one.
  • Help translate: a button in the language section (General tab) saves every text of the island in a file to translate into your language, or to review the one you use, and send in a new issue. A language with a reviewer says who. The file is written by the backup thread (BackupThreadProc), as the settings backup is.
  • A Share button on the shelf (and on each file under the mouse) opens Windows' own share window: Nearby sharing, Phone Link, Quick Share and the other targets (#7133). It's Windows' share UI for the island's window (IDataTransferManagerInterop::ShowShareUIForWindow), with the files as StorageFiles.
  • GlazeWM's workspaces can go on the pill, a dot each (the one shown lit, the ones with windows faint; a click switches), like komorebi's; "Hide the workspaces without windows" leaves out the empty ones (Control center tab, #7116). GlazeWM's own IPC, a WebSocket on 127.0.0.1:6123 (WinHTTP), only while the item is on.
  • Faísca, a little light that lives on the pill (#7045): an item of its own in every style, and on the minimized line too. Her eyes follow the mouse and change shape with how she feels (happy, angry, sad, startled, sleepy...), she blinks, does little things by herself, dances with the music of the apps you check and reacts to the PC (working hard, a low battery, Do not disturb, notifications, files copied, downloads, screenshots, the volume, USB, the charger, Wi-Fi, the song, Pomodoro, reminders), each reaction with its own switch. Her size can be chosen, her glow can leave the island (also over a maximized app) and the pill glows with her. All her options are in her own tab. There also: her color (eight, Windows' accent or your own, optionally changing with her mood), her personality (calm, normal or lively) and the processor use from which she counts the PC as working hard. She's drawn with Direct2D like the rest of the island, and her frames come from her own timer, only while she moves (about 30 a second, none when she's still).
  • Live activities like the iPhone's Dynamic Island (#7134). In Banners, turn on Live activities: the system alerts (charger, low battery, Bluetooth with the headset's battery, Do not disturb, desktop) show as a wide compact pill with the icon in a colored circle and the value at the right end, and optionally the apps' notifications in the same compact layout. And, with Expanded card, the mouse resting on what's live (the music, a timer or the stopwatch, a download or a copy) grows the pill in place into its card: the cover with the title, a bar and the buttons, the big time with pause and cancel, or the percent.
  • Five small games with Faísca (fruit rain, on the beat, cloud jump, island memory, reflex), with your best results kept on this PC.
  • Faísca's panel: click her to see her big, pet her with the mouse, tap her (not too often: she gets cross), read what she has to say, and open her games. Optional care: energy, food, water and love go down slowly while you use the PC, and you feed her, give her water and cuddle her there (she never goes away and never asks in full screen or Do not disturb). How fast they go down is a setting (calm, normal or attentive).
  • Sounds for Faísca, off until you turn them on: 25 sounds she makes (eating, a tap, a finished download, a plugged-in charger...), each with its own switch and its own source: the island's own, a pack downloaded when you choose it, or a file of yours. They stay silent over full-screen apps and with Do not disturb on. Her volume has its own slider. The island's own sounds are made by the mod and played with waveOut; a file of yours is decoded with Media Foundation, loaded only then. The pack comes from jsDelivr pinned to a commit (cesarkali/faisca-sounds@cec274c, CC BY 4.0), each file kept only if its SHA-256 is the one in the mod (BCryptHash), downloaded only when chosen. Never in full screen or Do not disturb.
  • What's playing: shuffle and repeat buttons (repeat all, then repeat one with a small 1, then off) in every look of the panel, shown only when the playing app supports them, like Spotify (thanks Jawad). From the media session's PlaybackInfo (IsShuffleActive, AutoRepeatMode), changed with TryChangeShuffleActiveAsync and TryChangeAutoRepeatModeAsync, shown only when Controls.IsShuffleEnabled/IsRepeatEnabled.
  • Faísca's panel says why she is as she is ("Dancing · Spotify is playing", "Hot · the processor at 92%", "Asleep · no mouse or keyboard for 6 min") and what she reacted to lately, with the time and her sound then: its name, or why it was silent.
  • A bubble saying when Num Lock turns on or off, like the Caps Lock one (Banners tab, off by default, #7178).
  • The processor's temperature can go on the pill, next to CPU use, only when Windows itself reports it (many desktops don't; Apps and tools tab, off by default). Read with PDH (\Thermal Zone Information(*)\Temperature, PdhAddEnglishCounter); without a thermal zone the item hides. No driver and no extra DLL.
  • What's playing's panel: two new options leave out the volume sliders with the mixer, and the two pill switches at its end, for a panel with only the player (thanks Jawad).
  • The timer and Pomodoro can fill the pill with color as the time runs out: orange, green on a break, fainter when paused, a soft pulse at the end, in every style and on the minimized line. Hide the numbers keeps only the icon on the pill, so the fill is all you see.
  • The Bar can have three parts: put two separator lines in the order (+ Line) with "Bar: items at the screen's corners" on, and the items before the first line stay at the left corner, the ones between the lines in the middle of the screen (the clock joins them when it is in the middle) and the rest at the right corner.
  • Tasks can have a date (#7195): turn on "Dates on tasks" and pick a day in the task's editor (Today, Tomorrow or any day). The day shows under the task, red when it passed, and the dated tasks come first. With "Tasks with a date in the calendar" on, the calendar marks those days with a small dash and lists the tasks in the day's list, where a click on the circle completes them.
  • Copy verification codes: a notification with a one-time code (like a sign-in or a bank code) gets a Copy code button on its banner and in the list. The code goes to the clipboard and stays out of its history (Notifications tab, off by default, #6997).
  • Faísca has fun too: with her care and her games on, a fifth vial that goes down while nobody plays with her. Bored and later sad, she now and then asks to play with two little hops and a pleading look on the pill (at most every 30 minutes, never in full screen, in Do not disturb or over a notification; it has its own switch). A round of a game cheers her up a lot, petting or a tap a little, dancing to music a tiny bit.
  • The island speaks French (Français), Turkish (Türkçe) and Korean (한국어), Windhawk's settings page too: choose one in the General tab, or it follows Windows. The first French texts are by 11ethann11 (#7063, #7186, #7228). The texts stay in the source, in the same packed tables as the other languages.

Improvements

  • The volume's percentage sits as close to its icon as the battery's (#6199).
  • The Bluetooth "Connected" notice shows the headset's battery when Windows knows it, like "Galaxy Buds2" with "Connected · 80%" under it (#6158).
  • Windows 11 only, 64-bit (x64 and ARM64): Windows 10, whose support Microsoft ended in October 2025, and 32-bit Windows are no longer supported.
  • Faísca costs much less while she moves: only the small area around her is drawn again and sent to the screen, not the whole island (in the Bar, the whole strip), on every monitor. Her area (m_petArea) is the only part cleared, drawn (an aliased axis-aligned clip, the rest of the bitmap kept) and presented (UpdateLayeredWindowIndirect with prcDirty) on her own frames.
  • If the island crashes and can't be started again by itself (on Windhawk 2.0, or after three crashes in ten minutes), a window says so and how to start it again: turn the mod off and on in Windhawk. It waits until a full-screen game or presentation is over. A TaskDialogIndirect on its own thread in Explorer, closed when the mod unloads. It only tells (nothing is started from it), and only for an island process whose image is Windhawk's.
  • With "Glow and hops can leave the island" on (or her size over 100%), each of her frames draws only her own window, no longer the whole island again behind her. The island remembers that her window was drawn alone (m_petWindowLast) and takes the full path again whenever anything else changes.

Fixes

  • Windows builds without the parts the dock uses (some Insider builds): the taskbar stays as Windows draws it and the island's taskbar parts (apps asking for attention, the screen-edge watch, the tray icons) now start right away, instead of waiting two minutes and giving up (#7241). ApplyToTaskbar counts a missing TaskbarFrame (g_dockUnavailable) as ready, so StartTaskbarParts runs (#7241).
  • Win+A and Win+N with Windows' own quick settings or notification center open now let Windows close them, instead of opening the island's control center or notifications over them (#7226). With an app run as administrator in front (Task Manager), Windows doesn't send the keys to the island at all: they work there only when Windhawk runs as administrator too. WindowsPanelInFront looks for Windows' own flyout before the island opens its panel.
  • The input method's bubble no longer shows up by itself when an app opens or is busy: when the app doesn't answer in time, the island keeps what it showed instead of taking it for English letters (#7260). The input method's state is asked with a time limit; with no answer the last known one stays.
  • A banner's title too long for its place keeps its "..." under the mouse until it starts scrolling, instead of being cut in the middle of a word.
  • Night light on a PC where it was never set up in Windows: the tile says Set up instead of Unavailable, and a click (also on the pill's button) opens Windows' Night light page with a short notice, since Windows only applies it after that first time.
  • Scrolling the settings window uses much less of the graphics card (#7282): dimmed switches and cards no longer draw a layer as big as the whole window on every frame, and the window draws at most about 60 frames a second. The dimmed parts' layers are bound to the visible area and the window's frames are capped.
  • The Wi-Fi panel, the control center's network tile and the pill's Wi-Fi icon show the connected network and its signal without location access too: only the list of nearby networks needs it (#7155). The connected network comes from WlanQueryInterface (wlan_intf_opcode_current_connection); where Windows refuses it without location access, the connection's profile stands in (NetworkInformation, GetConnectedSsid and GetSignalBars, read on a thread of its own). Only the nearby networks (WlanGetAvailableNetworkList) still need the location.
  • Tray icons of apps that run as administrator (many antivirus apps) now open with a click on the island even when Windhawk itself runs as administrator, and when an app still doesn't get a click, the log says which one.
  • The audio visualizer's bars now leave the pill when the player closes, instead of staying there until something else plays.
  • "Hide the Windows banners" is no longer greyed out while "The island handles notifications and their sounds" is on: it still hides the Windows banners that come through Do not disturb (calls, alarms, priority apps), so it can be turned off there too.
  • The What's playing panel opened from the visualizer once the player is closed shows "Nothing playing" on its own, without the last song's cover and artist (#7301).
  • The island no longer freezes for a moment when Windows is slow to say whether an app is in full screen: it asks on a separate thread and uses the last answer. SHQueryUserNotificationState sends a message to Explorer and waited up to ~400 ms in Island::Tick -> IsFullscreenAppOn up to 15 times a minute (all the islands share one thread), found by sampling the thread. Now the island asks on a thread-pool thread at most every 250 ms (TrySubmitThreadpoolCallback) and the callers use the last answer; the explorer part still asks directly.
  • The Bar no longer stays one strip below the top of the screen after a game changes the resolution (like 4:3) and back: the strip it keeps is set again for the screen's new size. The monitor rect the AppBar was set for is kept at ABM_SETPOS; Island::Render compares it with the monitor's now and sets the position again (SetAppBarPosition, Layout) when it changed.
  • With "The island handles notifications and their sounds" on, a reminder, call or alarm that Windows lets through Do not disturb (like a web app's notification that stays until closed) no longer shows Windows' own banner next to the island's while the pill is minimized or auto-hidden with "Banners even with the pill minimized" on: the island takes it over there too, with Windows' buttons. Chromium sends a notification that stays until closed as scenario="reminder", and Do not disturb's priority profile lets reminders through. The takeover decision (TakesOverBanner, used by CanTakeOverAhead and WantsTakeover) now also allows a minimized or auto-hidden pill when "Banners even with the pill minimized" is on, and minimizing or hiding ends a takeover that no longer applies.
  • The settings window's minimize, maximize and close buttons work again while the window is maximized (#7358): a click on them is now taken where Windows draws them, at the top right, and the middle one puts the window back. DwmDefWindowProc doesn't find the caption buttons of a maximized window with a custom frame. While IsZoomed, the panel answers WM_NCHITTEST and the WM_NCLBUTTON* messages itself for the 46 DIP buttons at the client's right edge (SC_MINIMIZE, SC_RESTORE, SC_CLOSE).
  • The dock no longer closes the Start button's right-click menu (Win+X) when the mouse moves fast from the dock to its options. It stays up and keeps the focus while a taskbar menu is open (#7360). GetGUIThreadInfo on the taskbar's thread (GUI_INMENUMODE, GUI_POPUPMENUMODE) for Win32 menus, and on newer builds a shown Xaml_WindowedPopupClass window on that thread while it's in front (the Win+X menu is a XAML menu there): while a menu is open the hide timer tries again every 300 ms. Only with auto-hide on.
  • "What's playing on the minimized line" now follows "Apps that bring the visualizer": with apps chosen there, the line's cover and bars show only while one of them is heard, not for any sound (#7343). MusicLineWanted asks the same chosen-apps list as the visualizer (MusicLinePlays).
  • "Apps that bring the visualizer" no longer lists one app twice when the media controls and Windows' audio know it under different names (Yandex Music had two cards): the card with the app's own icon stays, with your choice (#7301). Each audio session also keeps its packaged app ID and its Start menu name (read once per process), and a heard session joins the card of the same app.
  • On the left and right notches (Corners and Three), the minimized line stays near its corner instead of moving away when the notch grows, like while music plays (#7359). Island::LineMiddle keeps the line's middle at most 24 px (scaled) plus half the hovered line from the corner, as long as it fits in the notch; the small pill on the line follows it.
  • Explorer no longer crashes at sign-in on some PCs when the mod reaches the taskbar before Windows has finished making it (#7310). The 3.1.1 x64 fault offset (0x6b90) is XamlRootFromTaskbarHostSharedPtr reading a TaskbarHost that wasn't there yet; the chain (the TaskbarHost, its IUnknown, the TaskBand) is now checked for null, so the taskbar is left alone until it's ready.
  • The virtual desktops item no longer lists desktops closed long ago: on some PCs it showed extra ones that Windows still remembered, and renaming could pick the wrong desktop. In the island's elevated process the registry's VirtualDesktopIDs kept two desktops closed days before, while Explorer and other programs read one. With more than one ID read, each is checked with the desktops service's FindDesktop (already used for renaming, builds 26100+) on the watch thread: unknown ones are left out, the current one always stays, and all stay when the service knows none. Renaming takes the row's ID from the list shown.
  • With "Your own colors", the icons of the control center's switches that are on stay readable: a light highlight now gets a dark icon, instead of a white icon on white (#7431). The icon on a switch that is on is drawn in AccentInk (dark on a light highlight), as the other highlights' texts already were, not in the text color.

entry.title: Independent taskbar per monitor 1.7.0
entry.content:
• Fixed: window buttons of windows parked off-screen could appear on the taskbar of the leftmost monitor.
  • Fixed: clicking a pin could freeze the taskbar while the app's minimized window was busy.
  • Setting titles start with their section (Windows, Pins, Click, Animation).
  • Settings are available in English, German, Russian, French and Spanish.

entry.title: OverhauldedWin Alt+Tab 1.3.2
entry.content:
Added

  • Arrange open windows in an adaptive grid instead of the traditional horizontal carousel.
  • Automatically organizes cards into balanced rows, using up to four columns when space allows.
  • Grid: Navigate between cards using the arrow keys, with smooth selection animations.
  • Smooth scrolling with indicators when additional rows are available.
  • Added System, Dark and Light themes. System automatically follows the Windows app theme.

Improved

  • Window management:
  • Added smooth card repositioning when the window list or layout changes.
  • Improved selected-card scaling and visual transitions.
  • Refined the shared transparent background surface.
  • Improved the restoration of minimized windows when activating them.
  • Improved screen-coordinate handling for mouse interactions.

Other changes

  • Added additional activation diagnostics.
  • Improved timer error handling and logging.
  • Updated settings and documentation.
  • Added the required Windows system library dependency.
